Key: After each round groups split equally; after 20 rounds each of the 2^20 binary win‑loss patterns appears once, so all final scores are distinct → N = #tournament outcomes.  
Outcome count = ∏_{k=1}^{20}((2^k−1)!! )^{2^{20−k}}.  
(2^k−1)!! is product of odd numbers → odd. Hence N odd ⇒ v₂(N)=0.  
v₅(N)=Σ2^{20−k}[v₅((2^k)!)−v₅((2^{k−1})!)] >0, but v₁₀(N)=min(v₂,v₅)=0.  
Thus k=0, remainder 0. Pitfall: assuming ties; actually scores become unique.

Key: Final scores are distinct binary numbers → each round splits each group of size 2m into winners/losers. Winners set count = Catalanₘ (Dyck paths).  
N=∏_{j=0}^{19} Catalan_{2^j}^{2^{19‑j}}.  
vₚ(N)=∑_{j=0}^{19}2^{19‑j}[vₚ((2^{j+1})!)-2vₚ((2^j)!)-vₚ(2^j+1)].  
Compute v₂=524 287, v₅=121 818 ⇒ k=min=121 818.  
k mod 10⁵ = 21 818.  

Pitfall: assume ties—actually scores 0…2²⁰‑1 are all distinct.
